summary: Asked about a reel or post someone shared into an Instagram group, Nora no longer has a cover picture to settle for: the shared item shows up as its link only, so she reads the item itself.
details: A shared reel or post that comes with a valid link now appears in her conversation as who posted it and the link, with no picture attached. Before, the cover picture sat beside the link, and asked what was in a reel she looked at that one still and answered from it, even after being told it was only the cover.
The cover picture of such a share is no longer downloaded or stored.
A shared story keeps its picture beside its link, because the link opens the person's current story, which may no longer have the frame that was shared.
Asked about the cover picture of a reel or post shared before this change, she is told it is only the cover and pointed to the item's link, instead of describing the one frame.
An Instagram page link given without https://, or as a mobile m.instagram.com link, is recognised as a page too; for a mobile link she asks for the normal www.instagram.com link.

If she tries to look at an Instagram post, reel, story or profile link as if it were a picture, she is told straight away that it is an Instagram page and to open it with her Instagram reading tool, instead of the page being downloaded.
Her Instagram reading tool now introduces itself by what it gives back: every item in a post or reel, videos included. It is for anything somebody shares or links.
limitations: A share whose link is missing or not a valid Instagram link still shows its cover picture, since that is all there is to look at.
Shares from before this change keep their cover picture in her history; a story's is still served as a cover.
Whether she now opens the link is measured by routing cases that still have to be run against the deployed model.
